subject.title: fix(crestodian): run approval-intent classifier on the utilityModel, not flagship (#102360)

question: Should the current utility-model contract, including provider-declared small-model defaults when unset, classify ambiguous Crestodian approval replies before configuration mutations?
rationale: Code inspection can establish that the implementation is internally correct, but only maintainers can decide whether a lower-cost or different-provider model is an acceptable host-side consent classifier.

options.title: Accept utility classification
options.body: Sponsor this branch as canonical after the contributor adds real Crestodian proof for the selected utility model and fail-closed path.

options.title: Require explicit utility configuration
options.body: Revise routing so primary-model classification remains the default unless an operator explicitly selects a non-empty utility model.

options.title: Retain primary classification
options.body: Do not merge the routing change if ambiguous mutation consent must always be judged by the primary model.

recommendation.title: Accept utility classification
recommendation.body: Sponsor this branch as canonical after the contributor adds real Crestodian proof for the selected utility model and fail-closed path.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the classifier and surrounding host-side consent flow in merged history, making them the strongest available owner for the routing-policy decision.
